boundary_evidence: One contiguous run 0x0200f13c..0x0200f2cc, 2 functions, gapless in config/arm9/delinks.txt: func_0200f13c (main-engine BG2 and both engines' OBJ characters) and func_0200f220 (sub-engine BG2/BG3). Read from the highest address down (mwccarm emits .text in reverse source order).

SHARED DATA: each function indexes per-language file-ID tables of five words by GetLanguageIndex(), and the two functions' tables interleave in one .data run: data_0208a10c (func_0200f220), data_0208a120 (func_0200f13c), data_0208a134 (func_0200f220), data_0208a148 (func_0200f13c), data_0208a15c (func_0200f13c). config/arm9/relocs.txt has no other reader of any of the five. One object's .data cannot interleave with another's, so the five tables share one object; as each is read only by these two functions, that object is taken to be theirs.

AROUND THE TABLES: just below them are data_0208a0e0 (the player-count byte SetNumPlayers writes, initialized to 1) and the two per-language pointer tables data_0208a0e4/data_0208a0f8 the two scenes read. Just above is gMgGroupBase (0x0208a170), which only ov005 reads. None of the three is placed by these bytes: each could be this file's or a neighbour's.

BOTTOM EDGE (low address): GetLanguageIndex (0x0200f0bc..0x0200f13c) maps GetOwnerLanguage to the table index and touches no data. arm9/KuppaScript ends at 0x0200f0bc. Nothing in the bytes says whether GetLanguageIndex opens this file or is its own, so it stays out.

TOP EDGE (high address): func_0200f2cc (0x0200f2cc..0x0200f450) sets up the VRAM banks and BG controls the two loaders fill and has the same two callers, but it touches none of the tables. Call-graph evidence alone does not place a file boundary, so it stays out too. Hence medium confidence: the interior rests on private, interleaved tables, and the edges are the narrowest the data allows.
notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main. The schema follows arm9/Graphics3D.

No ROM name for this file: neither function has an SDK or RTTI name. The file takes its lowest function's name and stays under src/unnamed/arm9/0200 (tools/layout_check.py L3 wants an address stem there) until a name is recovered, as arm9/func_02073300 does. That is why the first function's legacy_source and the promoted source are the same path: tools/tu_promote.py moved the TU to src/unnamed/arm9/0200/unit0200f13c.cpp, and it was renamed onto the retired shard's path after.
Text-only: the five file-ID tables 0x0208a10c..0x0208a170 are this file's data but are not claimed here, so they keep their linker names and stay extern.
Both functions keep C linkage: d_s_entry_methods.cpp and d_s_mb.cpp declare them extern "C".
